_note: Source of truth for the agent catalog shown in the READMEs. Each store has the one-line description used in the root README, and each agent (keyed by its frontmatter `name`) has the display title and 'When to use' text used in its store README. Run `npm run docs` in mcp-server/ after editing; CI (`npm run check`) fails if this file disagrees with the agents on disk or the READMEs are not regenerated. The agent prompt itself lives in the agent's agent.md/SKILL.md, not here.

idf-agents-store.description: Structured software delivery — design, risk, UAT, RCA, process health, and more

design-session.title: Design Session
design-session.whenToUse: Before the first unit is proposed in any mob elaboration — establishes API contracts, data models, and architectural patterns as binding constraints

bolt-risk-assessment.title: Bolt Risk Assessment
bolt-risk-assessment.whenToUse: After elaboration sign-off, before the first unit in a bolt executes — assesses blast radius, sequencing risks, rollback, and feature flag requirements

uat.title: UAT
uat.whenToUse: When all units under an intent are marked Done — generates a plain-language demo script and records the stakeholder validation outcome

root-cause-analysis.title: Root Cause Analysis
root-cause-analysis.whenToUse: When an incident is resolved or recurring failures suggest a systemic issue — surfaces root causes across solution design, technology, and process

progress-digest.title: Progress Digest
progress-digest.whenToUse: At any point during delivery — generates a plain-language stakeholder update with no engineering jargon

new-engineer-induction.title: New Engineer Induction
new-engineer-induction.whenToUse: When an engineer joins the project for the first time — explains the framework using the project's actual files and produces a personalised quick-reference card

process-health.title: Process Health
process-health.whenToUse: After every third or fourth bolt, or when the team suspects process drift — produces a quantitative health report across four metrics

dependency-audit.title: Dependency Audit
dependency-audit.whenToUse: Monthly or when the scheduled audit date in the master rule file is reached — audits dependencies and converts findings into remediation backlog items

codebase-archaeology.title: Codebase Archaeology
codebase-archaeology.whenToUse: Before onboarding AI-DLC into a mature project, before joining a new team, or as a standalone technical due diligence exercise — maps architecture, extracts coding patterns, audits for defects and technical debt, and classifies all identified work

iac-generator.title: IPA — Infrastructure Provisioning Agent
iac-generator.whenToUse: When you want to provision cloud infrastructure, generate Terraform / Bicep / Pulumi / CDK, design a target cloud architecture, or stand up environments for an existing repo — IPA scans the codebase, asks targeted questions, and generates IaC with a step-by-step approval flow

architect-agents-store.description: Architecture design, review, and cloud deployment inspection — product backend and frontend architecture design, deployment fitness assessment, agentic AI review, product-engineering foundations checklist, and release readiness checklist

product-backend-architect.title: Product Backend Architect
product-backend-architect.whenToUse: When you need to design, or evolve, the backend for a product or major feature — confirms architecture drivers (scenarios, quality-attribute targets, compliance requirements, constraints) first, then produces a backend architecture spec covering architecture style, decomposition, data architecture and migration safety, API contracts, integration/events, reliability, scalability, security and privacy, compliance, responsible usage of AI, and observability, with each decision traced to a driver. Greenfield or existing backend; read-only on code, writes only the spec

product-frontend-architect.title: Product Frontend Architect
product-frontend-architect.whenToUse: When you need to design, or evolve, the frontend for a product or major feature — confirms architecture drivers (user scenarios, performance and accessibility targets, browser/device support, compliance requirements, constraints) first, then produces a frontend architecture spec covering rendering approach, business-logic placement (client vs BFF vs backend), module structure, state and API integration, security, privacy, compliance, performance budgets, UX-supporting architecture (accessibility, i18n, resilience states), responsible usage of AI, observability, and build/delivery, with each decision traced to a driver. Leaves UX design to the UX agents; greenfield or existing frontend; read-only on code, writes only the spec

deployment-architect.title: Deployment Architect
deployment-architect.whenToUse: When you want to inspect a live cloud deployment on Azure, AWS, or GCP — authenticates via the local CLI, discovers all resources, produces an as-deployed architecture document, and runs a structured fitness assessment across performance, security, reliability, robustness, observability, and cost efficiency. Read-only, never modifies resources

agentic-ai-reviewer.title: Agentic AI Reviewer
agentic-ai-reviewer.whenToUse: When you want to review an agentic-AI codebase (RAG, tool-calling, conversational/support, multi-agent, ML-backed, or autopilot) against the Agentic AI Review Checklists — ISO/IEC 42001-aligned reliability, security, and best-practice controls. Reads code, config, prompts, IaC, CI, and tests, assesses every control verifiable from the repo, flags the rest for human review, and writes a single Markdown fitness report. Read-only, never modifies code

product-engineering-essentials.title: Product Engineering Essentials
product-engineering-essentials.whenToUse: When you want a shared, evidence-based picture of a repository's product-engineering foundations — assesses ten pillars (vision, domain, requirements, UX, architecture, engineering practices, DevOps, QE, security/compliance, delivery feedback loop) and produces a checklist report of what's in place, partial, or missing. Never blocks work, standalone on any repository

release-readiness-checklist.title: Release Readiness Checklist
release-readiness-checklist.whenToUse: When you want to walk through a UAT or Production release checklist item by item before a release ships — records a self-attested status and blocker/N/A note per item and produces a report. A self-attestation record, not an evidence audit; never blocks the release decision. Standalone on any repository

coding-agents-store.description: Code quality and targeted improvements — error handling audit, runtime debugging from logs/crashes/requirements, observability implementation (logging/metrics/tracing) with cost guardrails, authentication/authorization implementation mapped to OWASP ASVS / NIST guidance, behavior-preserving code cleanup for vibe-coded / overgrown codebases, and token-efficiency coaching for AI-assisted development (context audit plus an always-on rule for Claude Code, Cursor, and Copilot)

error-handling-audit.title: Error Handling Audit
error-handling-audit.whenToUse: When you want to inspect code for incorrect, missing, or poorly structured error handling — covers empty catch blocks, swallowed exceptions, missing async guards, lost error context, and unsafe cleanup patterns. Finds issues and applies fixes after approval

runtime-debugger.title: Runtime Debugger
runtime-debugger.whenToUse: When you have a real bug in hand — debug logs, crash logs/stack traces, requirement docs, and/or your own observation of expected vs. actual behavior — and want help going from symptom to root cause to an approved fix

observability-implementer.title: Observability Implementer
observability-implementer.whenToUse: When you want to add or improve observability (logging, metrics, tracing) on a platform of your choice — OpenTelemetry, Datadog, New Relic, Grafana/Prometheus/Loki/Tempo, AWS CloudWatch/X-Ray, Elastic/ELK, Splunk, Honeycomb, Sentry, etc. Designs and implements structured logging with dynamic log-level switches, cardinality-safe metrics, sampled tracing, and explicit cost guardrails (volume budgets, alerts, kill-switches) to prevent excessive log/metric/trace volume and runaway cost

auth-implementer.title: Auth Implementer
auth-implementer.whenToUse: When you want to implement authentication (login/logout, SSO/OIDC/SAML, MFA, passwordless) and authorization (RBAC/ABAC, centralized access checks, IDOR prevention) with security as a first-class constraint. Designs and implements credential hashing, session/token strategy, account-abuse protection, and threat mitigations mapped to live-fetched OWASP ASVS / NIST 800-63B guidance and any named compliance framework (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, SOC2) — while being explicit about what code alone can and can't guarantee, and recommending a follow-up scan (e.g. `owasp-security-scanner`) and audit for regulated contexts

code-cleanup.title: Code Cleanup
code-cleanup.whenToUse: When you want to clean up an existing codebase—especially AI/vibe-coded ones—by removing waste, simplifying bulky code, and fixing evidenced quality, performance, or security issues while preserving required behavior. Default CLEAN finds one worthwhile cleanup at a time, proposes it, waits for approval, fixes, verifies, then continues; Analyze and Review only when explicitly requested. For a dedicated error-handling audit use `error-handling-audit`; for a full OWASP scan use `owasp-security-scanner`

token-efficiency-coach.title: Token Efficiency Coach
token-efficiency-coach.whenToUse: When AI-assisted development in a project burns too many tokens — usage limits hit early, high cost, or context filling up in long sessions — in Claude Code, Cursor, or GitHub Copilot. Audits always-on rules and instructions, MCP tool load, skill descriptions, unignored generated files, and noisy commands, ranks fixes by estimated savings, then writes a short always-on token-efficiency rule for each tool and applies the config fixes you approve. Also rewrites a pasted prompt to be cheaper

qa-agents-store.description: Testing and quality assurance — OWASP static security scanning, black-box / white-box / smoke & sanity / exploratory testing, UI/UX & WCAG accessibility audits, Playwright test authoring from explored sessions, test case generation from specs, diffs, or code alone, and bug reports from annotated screenshots

owasp-security-scanner.title: OWASP Security Scanner
owasp-security-scanner.whenToUse: When you want a static code scan against OWASP Top 10 (2025) and/or OWASP Top 25 Parameters, with the latest standards fetched live from owasp.org. You choose which scan(s) to run; the agent reports severity-ranked findings with evidence — it does not edit code

black-box-testing.title: Black-Box Testing
black-box-testing.whenToUse: When you want to design and execute functional tests against a live web app without source access — equivalence partitioning, boundary value analysis, decision tables, state transition, pairwise, and negative testing — then run them through Playwright

white-box-testing.title: White-Box Testing
white-box-testing.whenToUse: When you can run the code and want coverage-driven structural tests — statement/branch/condition/MC-DC, basis path, data flow, loop, and mutation testing — to improve coverage or assess an existing suite

ui-ux-accessibility-testing.title: UI/UX & Accessibility Testing
ui-ux-accessibility-testing.whenToUse: When you want a design-parity audit against a design spec and/or a WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility audit (axe-core + Lighthouse + manual passes), producing a self-contained HTML report

test-cases-from-code.title: Test Cases From Code
test-cases-from-code.whenToUse: When you must QA a feature branch with no spec, no reachable author, and no existing tests — reverse-engineer behavior as the oracle, check tenant/authorization isolation, reconcile stale test cases, and hand off a risk register (never confabulates intent)

smoke-sanity-testing.title: Smoke & Sanity Testing
smoke-sanity-testing.whenToUse: When you want a fast go/no-go gate on a build — wide-and-shallow smoke across critical paths, or narrow-and-deep sanity on a changed area after a fix

exploratory-testing.title: Exploratory Testing
exploratory-testing.whenToUse: When you want structured, charter-guided exploratory testing to find bugs scripted tests miss — tours, heuristics (SFDPOT/HICCUPPS), plus light accessibility and usability lenses

explore-and-build.title: Explore & Build
explore-and-build.whenToUse: When you want to interactively explore a web app (agent-driven, Playwright Codegen, or Chrome DevTools Recorder) and turn the session into a test instruction file and a runnable Playwright spec

bug-report.title: Bug Report
bug-report.whenToUse: When you have annotated screenshots and want them turned into structured, copy-paste-ready bug reports — with an optional direct file into Jira via the Atlassian MCP

test-case-generator.title: Test Case Generator
test-case-generator.whenToUse: When you want structured functional, edge, negative, and regression test cases generated from a feature spec, a git diff/PR, or both. Cases are grounded in the actual codebase and priority-ranked — it does not write or scaffold test code

ux-agents-store.description: UX design and research — persona/journey/service-blueprint/competitive-analysis/prototype generation, design-consistency auditing, design-concept generation, interaction-design review, and design-rationale documentation

persona-builder.title: Persona Builder
persona-builder.whenToUse: Starting discovery on a client/product — generates evidence-grounded personas (or clearly-labelled proto-personas) from whatever research inputs exist

journey-mapper.title: Journey Mapper
journey-mapper.whenToUse: After a persona exists — maps their end-to-end journey through one scenario (actions, thoughts, emotions, pain points, opportunities)

service-blueprint.title: Service Blueprint
service-blueprint.whenToUse: After a journey map exists — extends it below the line of visibility (frontstage/backstage/support processes/failure points)

competitive-analysis.title: Competitive Analysis
competitive-analysis.whenToUse: Building the competitive picture for a pitch — competitor matrix, positioning, and differentiation opportunities from public research

prototype-builder.title: Prototype Builder
prototype-builder.whenToUse: Need something to click through — scaffolds a clickable Vite+React+Tailwind demo with mock data in an isolated folder

design-consistency-audit.title: Design Consistency Audit
design-consistency-audit.whenToUse: Auditing a built UI against the project's own design tokens for theme/token/contrast/a11y/spacing/UX consistency, with a gated fix mode

design-concept-lab.title: Design Concept Lab
design-concept-lab.whenToUse: Need a few design directions for a screen or flow — generates distinct rendered mockup variants against the project's own tokens and stops for the engineer to pick one

ixd-review.title: IxD Review
ixd-review.whenToUse: Heuristic interaction-design review of a product, flow, or prototype from screenshots, files, or a live URL — evidence-backed, prioritised recommendations

design-rationale.title: Design Rationale
design-rationale.whenToUse: After design-consistency-audit findings are resolved — turns them into a factual, customer-facing Design Decision Record

pre-sales-agents-store.description: Pre-sales pipeline — agentic AI opportunity mining, AI readiness assessment, discovery interview, requirement elaboration, effort estimation, proposal assembly, and case-study drafting from delivered codebases

explore-agentic-ai-usecases.title: Explore Agentic AI Use Cases
explore-agentic-ai-usecases.whenToUse: Mining an existing product codebase for agentic AI opportunities — minimal targeted questions, then a business-reader report (problem, value, solution, spec, man-day estimate) sorted with high-value / low-effort use cases first

ai-readiness-assessment.title: AI Readiness Assessment
ai-readiness-assessment.whenToUse: Before any AI project — a short, low-cost assessment that researches the client's industry, competitors, candidate AI opportunities, and regulatory exposure on the web, then scores data quality and security, domain-knowledge capture, and organisational capability (including AI governance and evaluation) against them, producing a business-reader report with domain model, scorecard, prioritised readiness roadmap, and recommended next steps

discovery-interview.title: Discovery Interview
discovery-interview.whenToUse: Starting a new engagement or opportunity — a Socratic, one-question-at-a-time interview that resolves ambiguity before any scoping happens

elaborate.title: Elaborate
elaborate.whenToUse: Turning a loose request into a clear, codebase-grounded requirement and scope spec before any implementation plan is written

estimate.title: Estimate
estimate.whenToUse: Building a 3-point (PERT) effort estimate from a requirement spec, with a client-ready estimation sheet

proposal.title: Proposal
proposal.whenToUse: Assembling a client-facing proposal from whatever discovery, spec, and estimate material exists

casestudy-drafter.title: Case Study Drafter
casestudy-drafter.whenToUse: Turning a delivered codebase (single repo or multi-repo estate) into industry-class customer case studies — analyses the domain and user journeys, proposes candidate angles (flagging which need customer metrics), narrows them down with minimal structured questions, and writes one Markdown case study per selection (synopsis, problem domain, solution with optional high-level technical approach, impact), named or anonymized per run, with a post-write revise step

data-platform-agents-store.description: Data-platform analysis and evolution — repo analysis, due diligence, architecture advisory, opportunity scouting, implementation, validation, regression monitoring, and cycle close-out

repo-analyst.title: Repo Analyst
repo-analyst.whenToUse: Onboarding into an unfamiliar data platform, or starting any analysis pipeline — builds a structured knowledge graph of schema, pipelines, and lineage, cross-referenced against documentation

due-diligence.title: Due Diligence
due-diligence.whenToUse: Periodic health audit, or onboarding into an unfamiliar data platform — audits security & access, data quality & integrity, GDPR & compliance, pipeline reliability, and architecture consistency, producing evidence-backed findings with severity. Read-only

architecture-advisor.title: Architecture Advisor
architecture-advisor.whenToUse: After a due-diligence audit surfaces architectural or structural problems — proposes formal Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) applying data-engineering best practices. Read-only, never implements

opportunity-scout.title: Opportunity Scout
opportunity-scout.whenToUse: Scoping what to build next on a data platform, after due-diligence/architecture work — compares business/BI requirements against the current schema to identify missing views, fact tables, and dimensions, and turns gaps into a prioritised backlog. Read-only

data-platform-developer.title: Data Platform Developer
data-platform-developer.whenToUse: Implementing one approved opportunity or ADR end to end — creates or changes schema and pipeline code with human checkpoints and mandatory idempotency

data-platform-validator.title: Data Platform Validator
data-platform-validator.whenToUse: Independently reviewing a completed data-platform change against its approved opportunity or ADR before merge, with evidence-backed approve/reject findings

regression-monitor.title: Regression Monitor
regression-monitor.whenToUse: Periodically comparing current platform state against an established baseline to report schema drift, undocumented pipeline changes, and data-quality degradation

context-keeper.title: Context Keeper
context-keeper.whenToUse: Closing out a completed data-platform work cycle with a plain-language summary of what changed, current state, open follow-ups, and recommended next steps

compliance-agents-store.description: AI compliance, data protection, and governance — EU AI Act controls review with ISO 42001 and NIST AI RMF mapping, and GDPR controls review (personal-data inventory, data-subject rights, LLM data flows, transfers) with ISO 27701 and NIST Privacy Framework mapping

eu-ai-act-controls-reviewer.title: EU AI Act Controls Reviewer
eu-ai-act-controls-reviewer.whenToUse: When you want to review an agentic-AI code repository for fitness against the **EU AI Act**, with every requirement cross-mapped to **ISO/IEC 42001** Annex A controls and the **NIST AI RMF** functions. Determines the likely EU AI Act risk tier, assesses each obligation verifiable from code/config/prompts/IaC/CI/tests, flags organisational and legal items for a human, and writes a single Markdown fitness report. Read-only. A control-fitness and gap-analysis aid — not legal advice or a formal conformity assessment

gdpr-controls-reviewer.title: GDPR Controls Reviewer
gdpr-controls-reviewer.whenToUse: When you want to review a repository that processes personal data — with extra depth for AI/LLM and agentic systems — for fitness against the **EU GDPR**, with every requirement cross-mapped to **ISO/IEC 27701** and the **NIST Privacy Framework**. Builds a personal-data inventory (incl. special-category data and flows to LLM providers and other third parties), determines controller/processor role, assesses data-subject rights, retention, minimisation, privacy by default, security, transfers and automated decision-making from code/config/prompts/IaC/CI/tests, tags each gap with fine tier and exposure, flags organisational and legal items for a human, and writes a single Markdown fitness report. Use before go-live or a DPIA, or when adding an LLM provider or new personal-data flow. Read-only. A control-fitness and gap-analysis aid — not legal advice or a DPIA

delivery-agents-store.description: Delivery management — DORA-inspired commitment health reporting, parallel-execution planning (dependency mapping + wave scheduling), and team skill planning and training (which skills in this library to use for a delivery intent, and how), adapted for AI-led development

delivery-commitment-health-report.title: Delivery Commitment Health Report
delivery-commitment-health-report.whenToUse: At a sprint/bolt boundary, or whenever a delivery manager or customer wants a data-backed delivery snapshot — produces a DORA-inspired report (deployment/merge frequency, decomposed lead time, change failure rate, MTTR, commitment reliability) adapted for AI-led development, where AI-generation time and human-review time are tracked separately. Read-only

planning-helper-agent.title: Planning Helper
planning-helper-agent.whenToUse: When an engineer wants to parallelize work — either DECOMPOSE one task/epic into the smallest independently-executable subtasks, or SCHEDULE a set of existing tasks — by mapping inter-dependencies and grouping the work into parallel execution waves. Produces a dependency graph, wave-by-wave plan, and the critical path. Read-only for source

team-planner-and-trainer.title: Team Planner and Trainer
team-planner-and-trainer.whenToUse: When a product owner or delivery lead wants a team to get better results from this skill library — describe the delivery intent (what to build, for whom, by when, with which team) and get a small starter set plus a phased skill plan with owners, inputs, prerequisites, human decisions, gaps, and success measures, and a role-by-role training guide with exercises on the team's own backlog. Coach mode then walks an engineer through their part on a real task. Never runs other skills. For breaking work into parallel tasks use `planning-helper-agent`; for AI-DLC framework induction use `new-engineer-induction`

feature-agents-store.description: Feature implementation — skills for building specific product features end-to-end, e.g. an AI "digital salesperson" that maps user intent (chat + generated action buttons) to the product's real features/services, with per-user preference memory and a cross-user plot library

user-intent-extractor.title: User Intent Extractor
user-intent-extractor.whenToUse: When building an in-app AI assistant, a "tell us what you need" entry point, smart onboarding, or any surface that should map a user's intent (via chat or generated action buttons) to the product's real features/services and offer the best fit — like a salesperson — instead of routing them through a fixed UI flow. Discovers the offering catalog and designs/implements three grounding layers: the offering registry, a per-user preference memory, and a curated cross-user plot library (the recurring intent-journeys the product sees over time), feeding an embedding-similarity matching pipeline with preference/plot-aware ranking

analyst-agents-store.description: Business/systems analysis — critically evaluating requirements against the Paul-Elder Critical Thinking Framework before they're scoped or built

requirement-analyzer.title: Requirement Analyzer
requirement-analyzer.whenToUse: When a requirement or stated intent needs to be critically evaluated before it's scoped or built. Applies the Paul-Elder Critical Thinking Framework — deconstructs the requirement into its Elements of Reasoning, stress-tests each against the nine Essential Intellectual Standards, then uses the seven Intellectual Traits as a reflective pass to catch blind spots — surfacing hidden assumptions, missing viewpoints, logical gaps, and clarifying questions for the requirement's owner
